item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":126,"end_unit":127,"fact_summary":"Germany removed 659 Afghan nationals in the first half of 2023, but carried out no removals to Afghanistan during 2023; removals to Iran were generally suspended except for serious offenders and security risks, although four people were removed to Iran in the first half of 2023.","question_ids":["2B.4","3B.1","3B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 federal removal practice, with the Iran suspension originating in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policy to the German federal government and Federal Ministry of the Interior; it does not identify Olaf Scholz as personally directing each removal decision.","limitations":["The source gives no assessment of individual removal-case legality or outcomes beyond the reported figures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":127,"end_unit":127,"fact_summary":"In 2023, 9,028 Russian nationals applied for asylum in Germany, including 7,663 first-time applicants; the overall protection rate was 29.0%, up from 24.0% in 2022 and 15.5% in 2021.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 asylum applications and protection decisions.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern Germany's asylum system under the federal government, but do not establish a personal Scholz decision.","limitations":["The data do not measure the quality or causal effect of Scholz's policies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":127,"end_unit":128,"fact_summary":"Between 2022 and May 2023, only 55 of 2,500 applications from Russian men eligible for military service had been decided, and only 11 were decided positively in the first half of 2023; civil-society organizations attributed the low recognition rate partly to outdated country-of-origin information, while BAMF said its reports were revised in autumn 2023 and regularly updated.","question_ids":["3B.4","6B.2","6B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative decisions cover 2022-May 2023 and the positive decisions cover the first half of 2023; the information-update response occurred in autumn 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reported decisions and information-management response concern BAMF and the Federal Ministry of the Interior; no personal Scholz instruction is shown.","limitations":["The source presents competing NGO and BAMF assessments and does not independently resolve whether the recognition rate was erroneous."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":128,"end_unit":128,"fact_summary":"Germany's 2022 federal decree granted special residence and employment-related discretion to Russian cultural and media workers critical of the regime, including possible direct residence permits where return would endanger them; nevertheless, some Russian journalists in Germany reported receiving only tolerated status, limiting their livelihood and journalistic work.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","4B.3","4B.6","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The decree predates 2023 but its implementation problems were reported during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The decree was issued by the Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community; the source does not attribute its design personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source does not quantify how many journalists were affected or explain the individual administrative decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":128,"end_unit":129,"fact_summary":"After the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, Chancellor Scholz declared Israel's security a reason of state for Germany and stated that Germany stood on Israel's side in full solidarity; the government abstained from a UN ceasefire resolution and rejected an EU ceasefire resolution, while later government statements called for humanitarian corridors, protection of civilians, and compliance with international humanitarian law.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.3","2B.4","2B.5","2B.7","2B.10","7B.1","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns Scholz's October 2023 statements and the federal government's subsequent 2023 position.","ruler_attribution":"The declaration is directly attributed to Chancellor Olaf Scholz; the later diplomatic positions are attributed to the German government and Foreign Ministry.","limitations":["The cited report does not establish the operational effect of the statements on Israeli conduct or civilian protection."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":129,"end_unit":129,"fact_summary":"In late 2023, some pro-Palestinian demonstrations in Germany were prohibited without distinction as to the cause, which the report characterized as violating equal freedom of assembly; police responses were criticized as brutal and partly racially motivated.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.7","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the domestic political climate and policing after October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes actions by German local authorities and police; it does not show that Scholz personally ordered the bans or policing responses.","limitations":["The source does not identify the number of bans, jurisdictions, or final legal determinations for each incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":130,"end_unit":131,"fact_summary":"The federal government had declared in 2021 that it would no longer pursue the AnkER-centre concept, but such centres continued to operate in practice; by September 2023 BAMF was still present in nine AnkER centres, whose operating standards were set through varying federal-state and BAMF arrangements rather than a uniform legal framework.","question_ids":["4B.2","5B.6","6B.2","6B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The continued operation and BAMF presence are reported for 2023; the policy declaration originated in 2021.","ruler_attribution":"The stated federal policy concerns the German federal government and BAMF; the source does not attribute the continuation personally to Scholz.","limitations":["Implementation is substantially controlled by the federal states and local authorities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":132,"end_unit":132,"fact_summary":"During 2023, the federal states decided to introduce a payment card for asylum seekers; transfers to other cards or foreign countries were intended to be blocked and cash withdrawals limited.","question_ids":["5B.8","6B.2","6B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The decision and debate are reported as occurring during 2023, although the cited implementation report is dated January 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The measure was organized by the federal states, with federal policy context; the source does not show a personal Scholz directive.","limitations":["The source does not establish the final nationwide implementation or measured effects during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":133,"end_unit":135,"fact_summary":"Asylum-seeker benefits in January 2023 were set at €460 per month for a single adult outside accommodation centres and €413 for a single adult in an accommodation centre, approximately 82% of regular social benefits and below 73% for single adults in accommodation centres; civil-society groups criticized the differing calculation of basic needs.","question_ids":["5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The benefit rates and comparison are reported for January 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The framework is federal law administered with substantial state and local discretion; no personal Scholz action is identified.","limitations":["The report notes that the cited table uses rates applicable from January 2024 while labeling the comparison as January 2023, creating a date ambiguity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":134,"end_unit":134,"fact_summary":"Following a 2022 Federal Constitutional Court ruling that found no evidence that single adults in accommodation centres economized together, several states applied equal benefit treatment to single adults inside and outside accommodation centres; however, no corresponding federal legislative reform had been implemented by the reporting period.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.7","6B.5","6B.8","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The court ruling and state responses predate 2023, while the absence of federal reform remained relevant in the 2023 update.","ruler_attribution":"The ruling was judicial and implementation was primarily by state governments; the source does not attribute the lack of federal reform personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source does not measure whether all eligible individuals actually received corrected payments."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":138,"end_unit":140,"fact_summary":"German law allowed reductions of asylum-seeker benefits for specified categories, potentially removing pocket money and reducing benefits by almost half in some cases; reductions were limited to six months and required review, but courts and civil-society organizations questioned the constitutionality and discriminatory effects of parts of the regime.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.4","6B.3","6B.7","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal framework was in force during 2023, though several cited court challenges predate it.","ruler_attribution":"The rules derive from federal legislation and are administered by authorities; no personal Scholz involvement is established.","limitations":["The source states that reductions rarely applied during an ongoing asylum procedure and does not quantify 2023 applications of sanctions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":141,"end_unit":142,"fact_summary":"Asylum seekers generally faced a residence obligation limiting them to the district of the responsible foreigners' authority and could be required to stay in initial reception centres for up to 18 months, or up to 24 months under some federal-state rules; violations could affect benefits.","question_ids":["3B.5","6B.2","6B.7","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These restrictions were operative during 2023, although the main statutory extensions originated in 2019 and earlier state legislation.","ruler_attribution":"The restrictions derive from federal and state asylum law; the source does not identify a personal Scholz decision.","limitations":["The source describes the legal framework and examples but does not provide a nationwide 2023 count of affected persons."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":145,"end_unit":146,"fact_summary":"In 2023 the federal government expected to provide municipalities €2.8 billion for asylum-seeker reception and planned €1.3 billion for 2024; funding remained contested, with states and municipalities seeking more federal support.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.4","6B.6","8B.3"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The €2.8 billion expectation and the funding dispute directly concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The funding plan is attributed to the federal government; the source does not identify whether Scholz personally selected the amount.","limitations":["The report does not establish the amount actually disbursed or the resulting service quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":151,"end_unit":153,"fact_summary":"In 2023 reception capacity was severely strained: Berlin and Hamburg were around 97% occupied, Berlin required 8,000 additional places, and overcrowded facilities produced reports of cold tents, illness, inadequate sanitation, lack of privacy, registration backlogs, insufficient health care, and violent conflicts; the federal government and states agreed on additional federal aid in November 2023.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The capacity shortages, reported conditions, and November 2023 federal-state agreement concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the funding agreement to the federal government and federal states, while accommodation operations are primarily local and state responsibilities.","limitations":["The cited harms are drawn from multiple local reports and are not presented as a nationally standardized inspection result."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":154,"end_unit":155,"fact_summary":"A 2023 preliminary police count recorded 30 attacks on asylum accommodation centres through October, down from 65 in 2022, while attacks on migrants, asylum seekers, and refugees increased from 1,371 in 2022 to 1,515 in 2023; many attacks were classified as racially motivated.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The figures directly cover 2023, with comparison to 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern German police and federal government reporting; no personal Scholz action is shown.","limitations":["The accommodation-centre figure runs only through October 2023 and the source does not establish causation or government responsibility for the attacks."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":157,"end_unit":158,"fact_summary":"During most of 2023 asylum seekers in initial reception centres generally could not work; in practice the waiting period was often 18 months and up to 24 months in some states, while outside such centres employment after three months was discretionary; legislation drafted and adopted at the end of 2023 planned earlier access.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The restrictions applied during 2023 and the legislative change was drafted and adopted at the end of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The restrictions and proposed reform concern federal legislation; the source does not attribute the policy personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The report does not provide 2023 employment outcomes attributable to either the restrictions or the reform."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":159,"end_unit":159,"fact_summary":"In November 2023 the federal government approved the Job-Turbo programme, using a three-phase approach of language support, direct or coordinated job placement, and further training; benefits could be reduced when refugees did not cooperate as desired, and the report said effectiveness remained untested.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","6B.2","6B.4","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The programme was approved in November 2023; outcomes were not yet established.","ruler_attribution":"The measure is attributed to the federal government, not specifically to Scholz.","limitations":["The source explicitly states that comparative effectiveness remained to be assessed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":160,"end_unit":161,"fact_summary":"Although asylum-seeking children had a general legal right and obligation to attend school, regional rules delayed school enrollment by one to two months in some states and restricted participation; research found that federal-state regulatory differences strongly affected educational participation.","question_ids":["4B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The cited research and described practices were relevant during 2023, though some studies predate it.","ruler_attribution":"Education is primarily a federal-state responsibility; the source does not show a personal Scholz intervention.","limitations":["The evidence is based on research and state-level variation rather than a single federal outcome measure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":163,"end_unit":163,"fact_summary":"Beginning in 2023, all asylum seekers became eligible to participate in Germany's integration courses, which generally comprise 600 language lesson units and 100 orientation-course units; an earlier evaluation found only about half of enrolled participants reached B1 German proficiency, and researchers criticized course quality and teacher conditions.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Universal eligibility began in 2023; the evaluation evidence cited is from an earlier period.","ruler_attribution":"The eligibility rule and courses concern federal law and BAMF administration; no personal Scholz action is identified.","limitations":["The B1 result predates universal eligibility and cannot establish the 2023 reform's outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":164,"end_unit":165,"fact_summary":"For the first 18 months, asylum-seekers' statutory health care was generally limited to acute disease, pain, vaccinations, preventive check-ups, pregnancy-related care, and individually indispensable treatment; practice varied between municipalities, and critics reported that expensive diagnostic measures or therapies were not always approved.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The restrictions and reported administrative variation applied during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The framework derives from federal law and implementation by states and municipalities; the source does not attribute it personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source does not provide a nationwide 2023 measure of denied treatments or health outcomes."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The source is a broad country report; many facts concern federal-state or local implementation and therefore cannot be attributed personally to Olaf Scholz.","Several cited legal frameworks predate 2023 but remained operative during the target period; those temporal qualifications are stated in the relevant records."]}
